title: The claims ledger lock clears a stale lock file once, so two waiters never both hold it
goal: ledger_lock (in bl_base once ST-zqbo7xgc has moved it, else bl_dispatch) clears a lock file older than LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_S only when it is still the file it judged stale (an owner token or an atomic rename), so two waiters that both see a stale lock never enter the read-modify-write together, and a lone waiter still clears a crashed writer's lock

import os,sys,tempfile,threading,time,pathlib as P
sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import bl_base,bl_dispatch
L=getattr(bl_base,"ledger_lock",None) or bl_dispatch.ledger_lock
p=P.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/"kb-backlog-claims.json";lock=p.with_name(p.name+".lock")
lock.write_text("");os.utime(lock,(time.time()-3600,)*2);old=os.stat(lock)
A=L(p);A.__enter__()
real,once=os.stat,[True]
def stat(path,*a,**k):
    if once[0] and os.fspath(path)==str(lock):once[0]=False;return old
    return real(path,*a,**k)
os.stat=stat;inside=[]
def b():
    with L(p):inside.append(time.monotonic())
t=threading.Thread(target=b,daemon=True);t.start();time.sleep(1.5);early=bool(inside)
A.__exit__(None,None,None);t.join(30)
print("second waiter, holding a stale view, entered while the first held the lock:",early,"| entered after:",bool(inside))

gates.question: How does ledger_lock keep two waiters that both judged a lock stale from both entering: rename the lock away and compare its inode and mtime with the stat judged stale (put it back when it differs), or an owner token in every lock file?
